# pai worker

Run tasks on other providers: run, ps, follow, merge, providers, classes, config, ...

```
pai worker <command>
```

Workers are Claude Code runs on a provider you chose (cheaper, faster or local) that do one task while you keep working.
Start one with `run`, watch it with `ps` or `follow`, then bring its work back with `merge`.
Setup lives here too: providers, classes, config, policy, local, fallback, pool, proxy, mcp, on, off, install.

```sh
pai worker run --class implement -p 'Fix the retry loop'
pai worker ps
pai worker merge w-20260101-abc
pai worker providers
pai worker policy
```

See also: `pai providers`, `pai help worker run`

### pai worker run

Run one task on a worker (another provider or model)

```
pai worker run [options]
```

For local work use --local (picks the running local model); do not name a local provider.
Starts a Claude Code worker through the chosen provider and waits for it. The task goes in as -p '<task>' or, safer for long text, --spec FILE.
Options this command does not know (for example -p, --allowedTools) are handed to claude unchanged.
--label is the row shown in `ps`, `follow` and the status line; without it the first line of the task is used.
Give a worker an MCP tool by naming mcp__server__tool in --allowedTools; the server loads by itself.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider NAME` | string | — | Provider to run on (default: the active one, else the routing order) |
| `--class NAME` | string | — | Use the provider set for this kind of work (draft, implement, review, research, spotcheck, simple, complex, image) |
| `--role NAME` | string | — | Old name of --class |
| `--capability NAME` | string | — | Run on whichever provider serves this capability (see `pai worker capability`), e.g. image |
| `--for NAME` | string | — | Short for --capability |
| `--out FILE` | string | — | Where an image run writes its PNG (default: next to the worker log) |
| `--size WxH` | string | — | Image size for an image run, e.g. 1024x1024 (default 1024x1024) |
| `--timeout-ms N` | number | — | How long an image run waits for its answer (default 120000) |
| `--chain STAGES` | string | — | Comma-separated stages run one after the other, e.g. draft,implement,review |
| `--agent NAME` | string | — | Run the agent definition ~/.claude/agents/NAME.md on a worker |
| `--model ID` | string | — | Model for this run: default, fast or a model id (default: the model set for the class) |
| `--urgent` | flag | — | Needs a fast answer: go to the cloud even when the policy prefers local (see `pai worker policy`) |
| `--where WHERE` | string | — | Where to run: local, cloud or a provider name (local and cloud are resolved by PAI; same as the MCP delegation tools' where) |
| `--batch` | flag | — | This run is part of a fan-out: session-profile fallback skips targets below the profile's parallel_min |
| `--now` | flag | — | Go ahead of the runs waiting for a slot on the provider |
| `--force-local` | flag | — | With --where local: keep the run local even when the route classifier sends it to the cloud (infra/install/device/external tasks, 2 failed local attempts) |
| `--local NAME` | string | — | Run on the local model PAI resolves: the first running one in the class's routing tier order, else the workers.yaml `local:` preference when running (a `local:` that is not running is ignored), else the most recently used running model; --local NAME picks a specific running model |
| `--local-ok` | flag | — | This run may go to a local provider under the prefer-cloud policy |
| `--cloud` | flag | — | This run goes to the cloud under the prefer-local or auto policy |
| `--label TEXT` | string | — | Short task label shown in ps, follow and the status line |
| `--spec FILE` | string | — | Read the task from this file (or - for stdin) instead of -p |
| `--cwd DIR` | string | — | Directory the worker runs in (default: here) |
| `--mcp NAMES` | string | — | MCP servers or sets this worker may use, comma-separated (see `pai worker mcp`) |
| `--no-pane` | flag | — | Ignored: every start needs a visible pane |
| `--no-queue` | flag | — | Do not queue behind the provider's concurrent-run cap (workers.yaml maxConcurrent) |
| `--no-stagger` | flag | — | Do not wait for an earlier run on the same provider to warm its prompt cache |
| `--worktree` | flag | — | Work in a git worktree on branch worker/ID (default for implement and complex work in a git repo) |
| `--no-worktree` | flag | — | Work in place, no worktree |
| `--max-minutes N` | number | — | Stop after N minutes and keep the work (0 = no limit; default from the config, 60) |
| `--deadline HH:MM` | string | — | Stop at this local time (tomorrow if already past); not with --max-minutes |
| `--no-pool` | flag | — | Start fresh, never use the worker pool. Without it a run whose flags keep it out of the pool (own tool set, MCP, system prompt, stream-json, browser) is refused with exit 2 |
| `--browser` | flag | — | Allow browser tools |
| `--no-browser` | flag | — | Remove every browser tool from this worker |
| `--print-cmd` | flag | — | Print the claude command as JSON and exit without starting anything |
| `--report FORMAT` | string | — | Final report format: json or ag2 (default ag2) |
| `--no-report-retry` | flag | — | Do not ask once more when the final report is malformed |
| `--orchestrate` | flag | — | This worker plans and reviews; code edits are denied and go to local units |

```sh
pai worker run --class implement --label 'fix the retry loop' -p 'Fix the retry loop in src/net.ts'
pai worker run --provider glm --spec /tmp/task.txt
pai worker run --local -p 'Summarize the changelog'
pai worker run --where cloud --model fast --now -p 'Say hi'
pai worker run --chain draft,implement,review -p 'Add a --json flag to the export command'
pai worker run --print-cmd --class spotcheck -p 'Say hi'
```

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker follow`, `pai worker merge`, `pai worker resume`

### pai worker resume

Continue a finished worker with a new instruction

```
pai worker resume ID TEXT [options]
```

Starts a new worker on the same provider and model that picks up the conversation of a finished one (claude --resume).

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Id of the finished worker (see `pai worker ps`) |
| `TEXT` | yes | What the worker should do next |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `--output-format FORMAT` | string | — | text (default), json or stream-json, as for `run` |
| `--label TEXT` | string | — | Short task label (default: the old label with a return arrow) |

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker run`

### pai worker usage

Token totals per provider and model for a set of workers

```
pai worker usage [options]
```

Sums the exact tokens of the selected workers per provider and model: input, cache read, cache write 5m and 1h, output, plus the reported cost. A run's result event is authoritative when it carries totals; otherwise the assistant messages are summed (killed runs). Local providers are marked and carry no cost. This is the worker side of the A/B comparison; the top session's side is `pai audit tokens usage`.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--label PREFIX` | string | — | Only workers whose label starts with PREFIX |
| `--since WHEN` | string | — | Only workers started at or after WHEN (ISO time, or 1h / 30m) |
| `--until WHEN` | string | — | Only workers started at or before WHEN (ISO time, or 1h / 30m) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Machine-readable JSON output |

```sh
pai worker usage --since 2h
pai worker usage --label armA --since 2026-10-18T06:00:00 --json
```

See also: `pai audit tokens usage`, `pai worker ps`

### pai worker handoff

From inside a worker: pass a question or result to its parent

```
pai worker handoff JSON
```

Adds a message to the parent's inbox and, when the parent is running, says it to the parent. The payload is JSON: {"kind":"proposal|question|blocker","text":"...","data":{...}}. Sender and receiver come from the environment.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `JSON` | yes | The payload as JSON |

```sh
pai worker handoff '{"kind":"question","text":"Which branch should I target?"}'
pai worker handoff '{"kind":"blocker","text":"Tests need a database","data":{"table":"users"}}'
```

See also: `pai worker say`

### pai worker help

From inside a worker: ask a stronger model to do one sub-task (budgeted)

```
pai worker help [options]
```

Runs a bounded sub-worker (class implement, in place, 20 minutes at most) on a stronger provider and prints its report and the files it changed. Each orchestrated unit gets a small budget of help calls (default 2, PAI_HELP_BUDGET); past it the verb exits 4 and you report the blocker instead. Every call is recorded in help-ledger.jsonl; --report lists them.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--task TEXT` | string | — | The one-paragraph sub-task |
| `--provider NAME` | string | — | Provider to ask (default: workers.escalate.cloud.provider) |
| `--model NAME` | string | — | Model to ask (default: workers.escalate.cloud.model) |
| `--files A,B` | string | — | Files the sub-task concerns, comma-separated |
| `--report` | flag | — | List the recorded help calls instead of asking |
| `--scope ID` | string | — | With --report: only this unit |

```sh
pai worker help --task 'Rewrite the retry loop in src/net.ts to back off exponentially' --files src/net.ts
pai worker help --report --scope 20261018-0301-1
```

See also: `pai worker handoff`, `pai worker usage`

### pai worker merge

Merge a worker's branch into your checkout

```
pai worker merge ID [options]
```

Merges branch worker/ID into the original checkout, then removes the worktree and deletes the branch. With --verify (or the workers.yaml `merge.verify` default, which --verify overrides and --no-verify skips) the command runs on the merged tree first; if it exits non-zero the merge is reverted (git revert, never reset), the branch and worktree are kept, and the exit code is 1. A built-in stub scan always runs after the merge: added lines under src/ matching `TODO: implement`, `Promise.resolve(0) // TODO` or `throw new Error("not implemented` revert the merge the same way.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Worker id (see `pai worker pending`) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-commit` | flag | — | Apply the changes uncommitted; keep branch and worktree |
| `--patch` | flag | — | Same as --no-commit |
| `--verify CMD` | string | — | Run CMD after the merge; revert the merge when it fails (default: workers.yaml merge.verify) |
| `--no-verify` | flag | — | Skip the configured merge.verify default (prints a warning) |
| `--no-verify-tests` | flag | — | Skip the related-tests check (config workers.merge.verify) for this merge |

```sh
pai worker merge w-20260101-abc
pai worker merge w-20260101-abc --no-commit
pai worker merge 20261018-0301-1 --verify "npx tsc --noEmit"
```

See also: `pai worker verify`, `pai worker pending`, `pai worker discard`

### pai worker gc

Archive leftover worker worktrees

```
pai worker gc [options]
```

Moves old finished workers' worktrees into refs/pai-archive/ID. Before a worktree is removed, gitignored knowledge files (Notes/ and the like; not node_modules, dist, coverage, logs) are copied into the main checkout; a worktree that cannot be salvaged is kept. --dry-run prints what each worktree carries.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--older-than HOURS` | string | 24 | Minimum age of a finished worker, in hours |
| `--all-finished` | flag | — | Any finished worker, regardless of age |
| `--pool` | flag | — | Also remove leftover pool reserve worktrees (spare-*, slots/*) no worker owns and no process sits in (implied by --all-finished) |
| `--foreign` | flag | — | Also archive merged, clean worktrees of this repo that PAI did not create (refs/pai-archive/BRANCH); unmerged ones are kept |
| `--kill-orphans` | flag | — | End processes (pid + command listed) whose cwd sits inside a finished worker's worktree: SIGTERM, 3 s, SIGKILL |
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print what would be archived and what each worktree carries, change nothing |

```sh
pai worker gc --dry-run
pai worker gc --older-than 72
pai worker gc --all-finished
pai worker gc --pool --dry-run
```

See also: `pai worker discard`, `pai worker pending`

### pai worker kill

Stop a running worker

```
pai worker kill ID [options]
```

Stops the worker and every live descendant (the tree `pai worker ps` draws), leaves first: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if a process outlives it. Each saves its final state. A session may only kill workers it started (another session's worker is refused; --force overrides from the operator's terminal). A worker whose process id has been reused by something else is marked lost and nothing is signalled. --only stops just this worker.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Worker id (see `pai worker ps`) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--only` | flag | — | Kill only this worker, leave its children running |
| `--force` | flag | — | Kill another session's worker (operator's terminal only, not from a worker); logged as forced |
| `--reason TEXT` | string | — | Why it is stopped; recorded in the worker's event log and end status, required with --force on another session's worker |

```sh
pai worker kill w-20260101-abc
pai worker kill w-20260101-abc --force --reason "stuck loop"
pai worker ps   (find the id first)
```

See also: `pai worker ps`

### pai worker queue

Show or reorder the workers waiting for a provider slot

```
pai worker queue [VERB] [ID]
```

No arguments lists every worker parked behind a provider's concurrency cap, per provider in grant order (the order the capacity gate hands out slots in). `queue next ID` makes a waiting worker run next (position 1; `front` is an alias), `queue up ID` moves it one place up. The running worker is not interrupted: there is no preemption, only the order of the waiting ones changes. The waiting worker itself re-reads the order on its next poll, so a move takes effect within seconds.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VERB` | no | next (alias front) or up (default: list the queue) |
| `ID` | no | Worker id to pull forward (with next/up) |

```sh
pai worker queue
pai worker queue next 20261019-142851-84910
pai worker queue up 20261019-142851-84910
```

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker kill`

### pai worker wait-on

Wait for a background job to finish

```
pai worker wait-on PID [options]
```

Waits at most --max seconds (default 110, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) for a process id. Exit 0: it is gone. Exit 3: still running, call again. Exit 2: it never existed. Exit 4: killed by the ceiling or stall rule (its whole process tree gets SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5 s; likely a hang or infinite loop). A `pai worker run` target still queued behind its provider cap is not stall-killed (the queue prints a heartbeat at least every 60 s), and the ceiling counts from when it left the queue.
Recipe: nohup sh -c 'CMD; echo $? > /tmp/job.rc' > /tmp/job.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/job.pid, then repeat `pai worker wait-on $(cat /tmp/job.pid) --log /tmp/job.log` until it exits 0.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PID` | yes | Process id of the job |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--log FILE` | string | — | Log file whose last lines are printed on return; FILE.rc holds the exit code |
| `--max SECS` | number | — | Longest wait in seconds (default 110, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) |
| `--tail N` | number | — | Log lines printed on return (default 20) |
| `--max-minutes N` | number | — | Hard ceiling on the process's age (default 30; a queued worker run counts from leaving the queue): still alive then = kill its process tree, exit 4 |
| `--stall-minutes N` | number | — | With --log: log silent this long while alive (default 5) = kill its process tree, exit 4 |

```sh
pai worker wait-on 12345
pai worker wait-on $(cat /tmp/job.pid) --log /tmp/job.log --max 60
```

See also: `pai worker wait`, `pai worker wait-url`, `pai worker wait-file`

### pai worker wait-url

Wait for a server to answer HTTP

```
pai worker wait-url URL [options]
```

Polls the URL with backoff for at most --max seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically). Exit 0: it answered 2xx-4xx. Exit 3: not yet, call again.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `URL` | yes | e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8016/v1/models |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max SECS` | number | — | Longest wait in seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) |

```sh
pai worker wait-url http://127.0.0.1:8016/v1/models
pai worker wait-url http://127.0.0.1:8016/v1/models --max 60
```

See also: `pai worker wait`, `pai worker wait-on`, `pai worker wait-file`

### pai worker wait-file

Wait for files to appear

```
pai worker wait-file PATHS... [options]
```

Waits at most --max seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) until every path exists; prints one line per path. Exit 0: all exist. Exit 3: some missing, call again.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATHS...` | yes | One or more file paths |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max SECS` | number | — | Longest wait in seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) |

```sh
pai worker wait-file /tmp/job.rc
pai worker wait-file /tmp/a.rc /tmp/b.rc --max 60
```

See also: `pai worker wait`, `pai worker wait-on`, `pai worker wait-url`

### pai worker test-run

Run a test command; when it goes silent, say where it is stuck

```
pai worker test-run [options]
```

Runs the command (after --) with Node diagnostic reports enabled and passes its output through. When it prints nothing for --idle seconds (default 60, or 8 s before a `timeout N` in the command), every node process under it gets SIGUSR2 and the reports' javascriptStack is printed as the file:line the main thread is stuck in; an empty stack means an async wait. A synchronous infinite loop blocks the runner's own timeout, so without this a hung run shows nothing. Worker test commands (vitest, jest, node --test, npm test) are routed through it by the PAI guard. Exit code is the command's.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--idle SECS` | number | — | Silence after which the probe fires (default 60) |
| `--cmd-b64 BASE64` | string | — | The command line, base64-encoded, run exactly as given (what the PAI guard emits) |

```sh
pai worker test-run -- npx vitest run src/parse.test.ts
pai worker test-run --idle 20 -- timeout 120 npm test
```

See also: `pai worker wait-on`

### pai worker wait

Wait for child workers; returns when any finishes or --max elapses

```
pai worker wait IDS... [options]
```

Prints one JSON status line per worker id and returns within --max seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) as soon as ANY of them finishes. Exit 0: all done. Exit 1: a finished worker failed. Exit 3: some still running, call again with the unfinished ids.
Use this instead of sleeping and re-checking `pai worker ps`. --timeout keeps the old behaviour: wait for ALL, exit 1 on timeout (the same code as a failed worker; a timed-out worker's JSON has "state":"running", "timedOut":true and no "ok", and stderr says the worker is not affected).

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IDS...` | yes | One or more worker ids |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max SECS` | number | — | Longest wait in seconds (default 100, limit 590; over ~110 s needs the Bash tool timeout raised, which the PAI hook does automatically) |
| `--timeout SECS` | number | — | Wait for ALL workers, give up after this many seconds (exit 1) |

```sh
pai worker wait w-20260101-abc
pai worker wait w-20260101-abc w-20260101-def --max 60
```

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker wait-on`, `pai worker wait-url`, `pai worker wait-file`

### pai worker model

Show or set the model a provider uses

```
pai worker model [WHAT] [MODEL] [options]
```

No arguments lists the models of every provider.
`model MODEL-ID` sets the default model of the active provider.
`model CAPABILITY` shows one capability (default, fast, image, ...); `model CAPABILITY MODEL-ID` sets it.
`pai worker capability` chooses which provider serves a capability.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WHAT` | no | A capability name, or a model id to set as default |
| `MODEL` | no | Model id to set for that capability |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider NAME` | string | — | Provider to read or change (default: the active one) |
| `--capability NAME` | string | — | Capability to show or set, with the model id as the only argument |

```sh
pai worker model
pai worker model fast
pai worker model fast glm-fast --provider glm
```

See also: `pai worker capability`, `pai providers`

### pai worker capability

Choose which provider serves a capability (e.g. image)

```
pai worker capability [NAME] [PROVIDERS] [options]
```

No arguments lists every preference and what it resolves to now. `capability NAME PROVIDER[,PROVIDER...]` sets the list (the first usable one wins); `capability NAME --unset` removes it.
A provider of kind image preferred for "image" is what `pai worker run --capability image` calls.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | no | Capability name, e.g. image |
| `PROVIDERS` | no | Provider names, comma-separated, best first |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--unset` | flag | — | Remove the preference for NAME |
| `--json` | flag | — | Machine-readable output |

```sh
pai worker capability
pai worker capability image imagegen,backup
pai worker capability image --unset
```

See also: `pai worker model`, `pai worker run`

### pai worker providers

Providers workers can run on: list, add, remove, use, enable, disable, test

```
pai worker providers [command]
```

Without a subcommand, lists the providers. `use` makes one the active provider (the same command as `pai providers use`).
The configuration lives in workers.yaml (see `pai worker config path`).

```sh
pai worker providers
pai worker providers use glm
pai worker providers test glm
```

See also: `pai providers`, `pai worker classes`, `pai worker config`

#### pai worker providers list

List providers, their models and whether workers are on

```

```

Shows every configured provider with its models, cost tier and state. This is also what `pai worker providers` prints on its own.

```sh
pai worker providers list
pai worker providers
```

See also: `pai providers`, `pai worker providers add`

#### pai worker providers use

Make a provider the active one

```
pai worker providers use NAME [options]
```

The active provider is where `pai new` starts and where new workers go by default. Classes pinned to a provider are re-pointed.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Provider name from `pai providers` |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the exec line instead of executing |

```sh
pai providers use glm
pai providers use anthropic
```

See also: `pai providers`, `pai new`

#### pai worker providers add

Add a provider (the first one also turns workers on)

```
pai worker providers add NAME [options]
```

Adds a provider that workers can run on. The first provider you add also turns workers on and sets up the default classes.
Give the API token with --key (stored in workers.yaml, file kept private) or --key-file (path to a private file holding it), not both.
OpenAI-style APIs: --protocol openai --upstream-url URL (runs through the local proxy).
ChatGPT plan through the Codex CLI: --engine codex. Image generation: --engine image.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Name for the new provider, e.g. glm |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | string | — | Anthropic-compatible API base URL (required unless --protocol openai) |
| `--url URL` | string | — | Same as --base-url |
| `--model ID` | string | — | Default model id for this provider (required) |
| `--key TOKEN` | string | — | API token, written into workers.yaml; visible in ps and shell history, prefer --key-file |
| `--key-file PATH` | string | — | File holding the API token (kept private); leave out for a local server |
| `--fast-model ID` | string | — | Cheaper model for quick checks and routing |
| `--env NAME=VALUE` | string | — | Extra environment variable for runs (repeat for several) |
| `--note TEXT` | string | — | Short note shown in the provider list |
| `--protocol KIND` | string | — | anthropic (default) or openai |
| `--upstream-url URL` | string | — | Chat Completions base URL (required for --protocol openai) |
| `--engine KIND` | string | — | claude (default), codex, or image |
| `--context-window TOKENS` | number | — | Context window for the usage meter (default 200000) |
| `--quota-probe URL` | string | — | URL whose JSON first number is the quota percent (0-100) |
| `--cost-tier 1-5` | string | — | Cost tier: 1 (cheapest) to 5 (most expensive; default 3) |
| `--tags LIST` | string | — | Capability tags, comma-separated (from: code, vision, image-gen, long-context, fast, reasoning) |

```sh
pai worker providers add glm --url https://api.example.invalid/anthropic --key-file ~/glm.key --model glm-5.3 --fast-model glm-5.3-flash
pai worker providers add local --protocol openai --upstream-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 --model qwen
```

See also: `pai worker providers use`, `pai worker providers list`

|---|---|---|---|
| `--cost-tier 1-5` | string | — | Cost tier: 1 (cheapest) to 5 (most expensive; default 3) |

#### pai worker providers test

Check a provider answers — without a name, what workers would use now

```
pai worker providers test [NAME]
```

With a NAME, sends a tiny prompt through that provider and prints the reply and the time it took; exits 1 if it does not answer. Without a NAME it tests the provider routing would use for a worker now: the t2 tier's first available entry, else the active provider. The built-in `anthropic` provider is Claude Code's own login: it probes the local `claude` CLI (installed and logged in) and never needs an API key.

| `NAME` | no | Provider to test (default: what routing would use now) |

#### pai worker providers cap

Show or set how many workers run in parallel on a provider

```
pai worker providers cap PROVIDER [N] [options]
```

Without N, shows the provider's effective cap and where it comes from (config or default). N (>= 1) writes maxConcurrent to workers.yaml; `default` removes it again. Unset, a local provider runs one worker at a time and a cloud provider is uncapped.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROVIDER` | yes | Provider name |
| `N` | no | Parallel runs (>= 1), or `default` to unset |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | flag | — | Overwrite an existing workers.yaml |
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the plan without writing anything |

### pai worker policy

Where workers run: cloud, local, or a mix

```
pai worker policy [MODE] [options]
```

With no mode, shows the policy and the route the next run would take. A mode sets it; `clear` removes it (class and active-provider routing as before).
  cloud-only    never local (battery, on the road)
  local-only    never cloud (saves tokens); fails if no local server answers
  prefer-local  local first; a local run with a bad report is repeated once on the cloud
  prefer-cloud  cloud first (fast turnaround); local only when the cloud is unavailable
  auto          prefer-local, but cloud on battery and for an --urgent run
Per run you can add --urgent, --local-ok or --cloud; --provider beats the policy.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MODE` | no | cloud-only, local-only, prefer-local, prefer-cloud, auto or clear |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--for DURATION` | string | — | Expire the policy after 30m, 2h, 1d … |

```sh
pai worker policy
pai worker policy prefer-local --for 2h
```

See also: `pai worker local`, `pai worker providers`

### pai worker route

Print the routing table: per delegation tier the ordered models

```
pai worker route [ACTION] [CLASS] [MODELS] [options]
```

One row per delegation tier of workers.yaml `tiers:` (typically t0 Session: the interactive session itself; t1 Orchestrator: splits a job, plans, reviews; t2 Worker: implements the parts and runs quick checks), each an ordered list of models: the first available one serves, the rest is the fallback order (a tier is not a fallback rank). The first line is the flow, what each tier resolves to right now. Local models ("local gyro-m") are entries like any other; one whose server is not running is skipped, never started. `pai worker policy` rewrites the default tier's list.
`route set <tier|class> <provider/model,...>` sets a row (a class sets its tier's row): a cloud entry is provider/model (glm/glm-5.3-flash, anthropic/opus, glm/fast), a local one the provider name (gyro-m). --note adds the reason (tooltip). Tiers, their classes and descriptions are edited in workers.yaml.
--session <name|self> makes it a per-session override stored in that session's profile (`route set --session s <tier|class> <models>`, `route clear --session s [<tier|class>]`); runs started from that session use its row, else the global one. `route --session s` prints the effective table for that session.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTION` | no | set or clear (omit to print) |
| `CLASS` | no | A tier id (t0, t1, t2, ... as configured) or a class (it sets its tier) |
| `MODELS` | no | Comma-separated provider/model entries, first serves |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--session NAME` | string | — | Per-session override: a session name or self |
| `--note TEXT` | string | — | Reason for the row (tooltip), e.g. "context width, reasoning" |

```sh
pai worker route
pai worker route set t2 gyro-m,anthropic/sonnet,glm/glm-5.3-flash --note "context width, reasoning"
pai worker route set --session self t2 anthropic/sonnet
pai worker route clear --session self t2
pai worker route --session self
```

See also: `pai worker policy`, `pai worker classes`

### pai worker local

Which local models run; the operator starts and stops them

```
pai worker local [TARGET] [NAME] [options]
```

Without TARGET: one line with the running local model (the daemon's answer, `--local` runs on it). Sessions never probe ports or start servers.
  start MODEL [--count N]   start N more instances of MODEL (own port each; refused when memory or maxInstances is short; --force skips the memory check)
  stop MODEL|ID [--count N | --all]   stop instances (highest number first); refused while requests are in flight unless --yes
  status                    what is up
  off                       stop every local server
  MODEL                     deprecated alias of `start MODEL` (kept one release). It no longer stops the other models first.
Models are listed under local_tiers: in workers.yaml. This does not change where workers are routed (see `pai worker policy`).

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TARGET` | no | start, stop, status, off, or a model name; omit for the running local model |
| `NAME` | no | The model (start) or model / instance id (stop) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the exact commands without starting or stopping anything |
| `--count N` | string | — | start / stop: how many instances (default 1) |
| `--all` | flag | — | stop: every instance of the model |
| `--force` | flag | — | start: skip the memory check |
| `--yes` | flag | — | stop: even with requests in flight |

```sh
pai worker local
pai worker local status
pai worker local start big --count 2
pai worker local stop big#2
pai worker local off
```

See also: `pai worker policy`, `pai worker config path`

Run every new Claude Code process on a worker provider


`on [PROVIDER]` switches (default: the active provider) by writing env and a model pin into settings.json; `off` restores settings.json exactly; `status` shows the state and running sessions (also the default).
Set CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH to another settings.json for a dry run.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTION` | no | on, off or status (default: status) |
| `PROVIDER` | no | With on: provider to switch to |

```sh
pai worker fallback status
CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH=/tmp/settings.json pai worker fallback on glm
```

See also: `pai worker providers use`, `pai worker policy`

Long-lived headless claude slots that successive small runs talk to, so the provider's prompt cache carries over.
`on` starts the background host and enables routing, `off` stops both, `status` (default) shows slots, tasks served and cache savings. Default is off.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTION` | no | on, off or status (default: status) |

```sh
pai worker pool status
pai worker pool on
```

See also: `pai worker on`

### pai worker on

Send Agent-tool subagents to workers

```
pai worker on
```

Turns worker routing on (the default once a provider exists). The Agent hook then denies the Agent tool and suggests `pai worker run`.

```sh
pai worker on
pai worker off
```

See also: `pai worker off`

### pai worker off

Stop routing: Agent tool runs on Anthropic again

```
pai worker off
```

Turns worker routing off. Subagents started with the Agent tool run on Anthropic as usual.

```sh
pai worker off
pai worker on
```

See also: `pai worker on`

### pai worker install

Set up the Agent hook and command shims

```
pai worker install
```

Adds the Agent hook to settings.json, writes the glm* shims in ~/.local/bin and cleans up old scripts. Safe to run again.

```sh
pai worker install
pai worker providers
```

See also: `pai worker on`

### pai worker controls

Hand the desktop controls to a worker, or take them back

```
pai worker controls ID WHO
```

WHO is `you` (the worker becomes the exclusive holder of the desktop controls; needs clickr with --agent support) or `me` (you take them back).
Inside a worker's pane, typing "your controls" does the same.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Worker id (see `pai worker ps`) |
| `WHO` | yes | you or me |

```sh
pai worker controls 20260101-120000-1234 you
pai worker controls 20260101-120000-1234 me
```

See also: `pai worker ps`

### pai worker bench

Compare providers on a set of real tasks

```
pai worker bench [options]
```

For each task × provider × repeat, runs the suite's run.sh and then grade.sh, prints pass counts, median time and turns per provider, and writes results.md into the suite folder.
Providers are named explicitly: a measurement ignores `pai worker policy`.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--suite DIR` | string | — | Suite folder with run.sh, grade.sh and tasks/NAME/ (required) |
| `--providers LIST` | string | — | Comma-separated providers, e.g. anthropic,local30 |
| `--tasks LIST` | string | — | Comma-separated task names (default: all) |
| `--prompt KIND` | string | task | Prompt file kind: task|spec|precise |
| `--repeat N` | string | 1 | Runs per task and provider |
| `--max-parallel N` | string | 3 | Runs going at once |
| `--max-load N` | string | 60 | Start no run while the 1-minute load average is above this |
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Print the plan only |
| `--report` | flag | — | Only summarise the suite's existing rows.tsv into results.md; run nothing |

```sh
pai worker bench --suite ./suite --providers anthropic,glm --dry-run
pai worker bench --suite ./suite --report
```

See also: `pai worker providers`

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai worker run` | Run one task on a worker (another provider or model) |
| `pai worker resume` | Continue a finished worker with a new instruction |
| `pai worker ps` | List this session's workers, running and finished |
| `pai worker usage` | Token totals per provider and model for a set of workers |
| `pai worker follow` | Watch a worker live, or all running workers |
| `pai worker replay` | Print the transcript of one worker |
| `pai worker watch` | Worker list that refreshes every 2 seconds |
| `pai worker pane` | Open a window pane that follows a worker |
| `pai worker log` | Worker ledger or the raw events of one worker |
| `pai worker errors` | Tool errors workers hit, grouped by kind |
| `pai worker status-line` | One-line worker summary for a status bar |
| `pai worker say` | Send a message to a running worker |
| `pai worker goal` | Leave a goal note on a running worker |
| `pai worker handoff` | From inside a worker: pass a question or result to its parent |
| `pai worker help` | From inside a worker: ask a stronger model to do one sub-task (budgeted) |
| `pai worker merge` | Merge a worker's branch into your checkout |
| `pai worker verify` | Check that a worker's changes are already in your checkout |
| `pai worker pending` | Finished workers whose work is not merged yet |
| `pai worker discard` | Throw away a worker's branch and worktree |
| `pai worker gc` | Archive leftover worker worktrees |
| `pai worker kill` | Stop a running worker |
| `pai worker queue` | Show or reorder the workers waiting for a provider slot |
| `pai worker wait-on` | Wait for a background job to finish |
| `pai worker wait-url` | Wait for a server to answer HTTP |
| `pai worker wait-file` | Wait for files to appear |
| `pai worker test-run` | Run a test command; when it goes silent, say where it is stuck |
| `pai worker wait` | Wait for child workers; returns when any finishes or --max elapses |
| `pai worker model` | Show or set the model a provider uses |
| `pai worker capability` | Choose which provider serves a capability (e.g. image) |
| `pai worker providers` | Providers workers can run on: list, add, remove, use, enable, disable, test |
| `pai worker classes` | Which provider serves draft, implement, review, … |
| `pai worker roles` | Old name of `classes` |
| `pai worker config` | The workers.yaml file itself: path, init, migrate, check, inline-keys, normalize-paths |
| `pai worker policy` | Where workers run: cloud, local, or a mix |
| `pai worker route` | Print the routing table: per delegation tier the ordered models |
| `pai worker local` | Which local models run; the operator starts and stops them |
| `pai worker fallback` | Run every new Claude Code process on a worker provider |
| `pai worker pool` | Keep headless worker sessions warm between small runs |
| `pai worker proxy` | The local proxy for OpenAI-style providers |
| `pai worker mcp` | MCP servers workers may load |
| `pai worker on` | Send Agent-tool subagents to workers |
| `pai worker off` | Stop routing: Agent tool runs on Anthropic again |
| `pai worker install` | Set up the Agent hook and command shims |
| `pai worker controls` | Hand the desktop controls to a worker, or take them back |
| `pai worker bench` | Compare providers on a set of real tasks |

## Examples

```bash
# Where do workers run? One persistent switch (stored in <logDir>/routing-policy.json)
pai worker policy                 # show the policy and the route a plain run takes now
pai worker policy prefer-local    # local first, cloud when local is down or its report fails
pai worker policy cloud-only --for 2h   # on the road: never local, back to normal after 2 h
pai worker policy clear           # no policy: class/active routing as before

# Per run (--provider still beats the policy)
pai worker run --urgent --class implement --spec task.txt    # fast turnaround -> cloud
pai worker run --cloud ...        # this run to the cloud under prefer-local/auto
pai worker run --local-ok ...     # this run may go local under prefer-cloud
```

**Routing policy.** `cloud-only` never uses a local provider; `local-only` never uses the cloud
and fails when no local server answers; `prefer-local` tries the first enabled loopback provider
(one `/v1/models` ping, 4 s: a busy server answers slowly) and uses the cloud when none answers or none is configured;
`prefer-cloud` uses the cloud and goes local only when the cloud is in cooldown or over its quota
(or on `--local-ok`); `auto` is `prefer-local`, but cloud on battery (`pmset -g batt`) and for an
`--urgent` run. The chosen route and its reason (`policy prefer-local`, `battery`, `urgent`,
`local down`, `no local provider`, `fall-through (…)`) are stored in the worker status and shown
by `pai worker ps`.

**Fall-through.** Under every policy but `local-only`, a local run whose report is invalid, was
downgraded by the proof check (`claimed proof not run`), is `r=-` or `r=!`, ended without a
report, or hit its max-minutes is repeated once on the cloud as a new worker labelled
`… (fall-through)`. The two statuses link each other (`fell through to <id>`, `fall-through of
<id>`). Local models are right when the spec names cause and owner; for diagnosis from symptoms
use `--cloud` or `--provider`.
